findingDetails.title: Backtick symlink rule accepts a target outside the repository or a missing target; the link check rejects the same target
findingDetails.claim: pathPresent treats any symlink as present (existsSync OR lstat isSymbolicLink) with no containment check, so a backticked path whose symlink target lies outside the repository, or is missing, suppresses BACKTICK_PATH_UNRESOLVED, while the same target behind a markdown link is rejected by pathChecks through realpath containment (PATH_SYMLINK_OUTSIDE_RE) or PATH_MISSING.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: read every pathPresent caller (only backtickPathChecks:416); confirmed the tests pin only the dangling in-repo case (no out-of-repo containment case); symlink census of 468 tracked links found 4 resolving outside the worktree, all under specs/** review scratch and none introduced by this diff, so the accepted target class is real in-tree.
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: accepting the unbuilt-build-output symlink (.opencode/plugins/sk-vision.js -> ../skills/sk-vision/vision-runtime/dist/plugin.js, target missing in a fresh checkout) is the rule's stated purpose, so target existence cannot be required; but nothing in that purpose requires accepting targets outside the repository.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: pathPresent gains containment (lexical in-repo containment for dangling targets, realpath containment for live ones) or the rule is restricted to tracked in-repo symlinks.
findingDetails.recommendation: Mirror pathChecks in pathPresent: resolve the declared target lexically against the link directory and require repository containment for missing targets; require realpath containment when the target exists; add the out-of-repo case beside the dangling case in the test set.
